nl · Oct 17, 2026

I agree that "frontier model" really does mean "pushing the frontier of intelligence", so Fable or Astra.

They might mean the intelligence/dollar frontier aka the Pareto frontier, but honestly much of the time that's not a great measure.

If you are doing repeated work on the same task (eg call center triage) then you can always beat a large LLM on price by fine tuning a small one.

If you are doing knowledge work then models are so varied that factors other than price are usually important. For example, lots of people moved away from Opus 5 because of it's awful English, whereas Opus 5.5 has fixed that. These things aren't measured in benchmarks.

How much is 6.5% percent concretely though? Assuming the six benchmarks have ~30 tasks each (180 in total), and we're doing 120 tok/s lets say, time/task for GLM-5.3 Flash would be ~25 minutes and this "token efficient fine-tune" would arrive at ~23 minutes.

Again, a 6.5% difference is highlighted as the most impactful change for this fine-tune, but it's a marginal difference. They're definitely trying to mislead people into thinking this is something more than it is, otherwise this landing page would have been much more realistic and less self-patted.
